title: Perturbed Metrics in the Poincaré Ball: Volume Bounds, Matrix Jacobi Fields, and Stability of Finite-Scale Geometric Indices
content: We study the geometry of the Poincaré ball equipped with a rotationally symmetric metric \(g_\eta\) conformally close to the hyperbolic metric \(g_{\mathbb{H}}\), with curvature pinched in \([-1-\eta, -1+\eta]\). We work with the matrix Jacobi field \(A_\eta\) and the shape operator \(S_\eta = A_\eta' A_\eta^{-1}\), whose trace \(\sigma_\eta = \operatorname{tr} S_\eta\) satisfies a Riccati equation. For rotationally symmetric non-homogeneous metrics and centres \(z \neq 0\), the geodesic spheres need not be isotropic: the volume element in geodesic polar coordinates centred at \(z\) is generally \(\det A_\eta(t, \omega, z)\,dt\,d\omega\), not a power of a scalar radial profile. Five results are established under the stated assumptions. First, using Günther and Bishop--Gromov comparison, we prove two-sided model-volume bounds \[ V_{-(1-\eta)}^{\mathrm{model}}(\delta) \le V_\eta(\delta, z) \le V_{-(1+\eta)}^{\mathrm{model}}(\delta) \] uniformly in \(z\). Second, we prove an exact weighted-average identity for \(\Sigma_\eta(\delta, z) = \partial_\delta\log \partial_\delta V_\eta(\delta, z)\), in which the anisotropy of the geodesic spheres enters as a positive variance term. Third, we prove a monotonicity-transfer lemma: if \(q_\eta(\delta, z) = \delta\,\Sigma_\eta(\delta, z)\) is strictly increasing in \(\delta\), then the volume indicator \(\phi_\eta(\delta, z) = \delta\,\partial_\delta V_\eta/V_\eta\) is strictly increasing. Fourth, under two explicit assumptions on the metric family — a global \(C^2\)-closeness to \(g_{\mathbb{H}}\) and a uniform \(O(\eta)\)-stability of the logarithm map along a compact family of endpoint pairs — we prove \(C^1\)-stability of the perturbed radial step \(\delta_+^\eta(r, \varepsilon)\) on compact radial intervals. Fifth, we prove an invariant LID bridge for \(g_\eta\)-Lipschitz densities. The local monotonicity of \(\phi_\eta\) on \((0, D]\) is stated as a conditional result under an explicit averaged-Riccati positivity assumption, which we do not prove; the global version is not resolved by our method.
